ca_solo_rock.blurb: Solo Rock is a very small formation at roughly 7,200 feet in the San Bernardino Mountains, just beyond Kindergarten Rock in the Children's Forest group of cliffs. It has nine climbs, split between five boulder problems and four trad lines. The problems run from the easiest grade up to V2, and the roped climbs stay between the mid-5.6 range and 5.9, so it suits beginners and anyone working on first placements. The rock is coarse and grainy like the other cliffs on Keller Peak. The formation is short, which makes it a stop to combine with its neighbours rather than a full day on its own.

ca_shirtsleeve_rock.blurb: Shirtsleeve Rock is a small crag at about 7,160 feet in the San Bernardino Mountains, tucked behind Hungover Wall near Keller Peak. It has two faces: one carries five trad routes, spotted from Hungover Wall by a wide crack near its edge, and the other holds three moderate sport climbs. Nine climbs in all, including one boulder problem, spanning the low 5.x grades up to 5.10, with the bulk around 5.8 to 5.10. The rock is very coarse, so expect abrasive holds. It sits close to the road, so it pairs easily with a day at the neighbouring wall.
ca_shirtsleeve_rock.parking_note: Drive 3.4 miles up Keller Peak Road and look for the lot on the left-hand side as you climb. It holds about four or five cars, with extra room a little farther up the road.

ca_ao_this_and_that_cliff.blurb: This and That Cliff is a small crag in the Lower Merced River Canyon, downstream of Yosemite Valley along Highway 140 at about 3,800 feet. It has nine climbs, mostly trad, plus a single sport route and one boulder problem. The grades are on the harder side: roped climbs run from 5.9 up to the low 5.12 range, with several in the 5.10 and 5.11 bands, and one trad and aid line. One route is a three-pitch outing. The approach shares a trail with two neighbouring crags, and poison oak grows beside the path to the trad side, so long sleeves help.

ca_tendon_damage_boulder.blurb: Tendon Damage Boulder is a squat, rounded block at about 6,100 feet in the Snow Valley bouldering zone above Running Springs, part of the Incognito Boulders. Nine problems, all of them low-grade: five at the easiest grade, three around V0, and one at V2. Most are moderate slab problems that reward footwork over power. Holds are rounded and sloping, landings are mostly flat, and heights are modest. A few lines have gone dirty and collect pine needles. It works well for beginners or as a warm-up stop near the parking area.

ca_thunder_wall_boulder.blurb: Thunder Wall Boulder is a long block on the Druid Stone side of the Thunder Wall Area near Bishop, at about 6,200 feet in the Eastern Sierra. Its main face is a slightly overhanging wall coated in orange patina, with crimpy lines on small edges. There are nine problems, one at each grade from V3 up to V11, so moderates sit beside a handful of hard testpieces. To find it, follow the path around the left side of the Druid Stone until the long patina wall comes into view.

ca_two_tree_rock.blurb: Two Tree Rock is a broad, plain-looking block at about 7,400 feet in the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles, close to Big Bear Lake in the San Bernardino Mountains. It takes its name from the pair of small trees on top. Climbs lie on two faces, with the longest and cleanest wall facing west; that wall sees shade early in the day and sun from midday on, depending on the section. There are nine routes, six trad and three sport, from walk-up terrain through 5.10, with four of them in the 5.10 range. It is a short walk from the Pinnacles South parking.

ca_voodoo_dome.blurb: Voodoo Dome is a smaller dome on the western slope of the southern Sierra Nevada, at about 7,500 feet, standing between Big Sleep and Crocodile Dome. It sees fewer climbers than its larger neighbour. There are nine routes, eight of them trad and one sport, nearly all in the 5.10 range, with one at 5.9 and one in the 5.11 band. The setting is similar to the rest of the Big Sleep area, with a trail junction near the wash marking the turn toward the dome. Expect a moderate to hard day of crack and face climbing rather than beginner terrain.

ca_wall_of_glass_area.blurb: Wall of Glass Area is a bouldering zone on the western face of Mount Rubidoux in Riverside, at about 870 feet. The boulders are scattered low on the hill, away from the road to the summit cross where most of Rubidoux's traffic goes. There are nine problems across three small clusters. Most are easy to moderate, with a few around V4 and V5 and one much harder line. Friction is the theme, from blank slabs to a couple of tall, run-out faces. The ground can be dirty and overgrown.

_conflicts.ca_wall_of_glass_area: Stored rock is granite; the Mount Rubidoux parent page (https://www.mountainproject.com/v/mount-rubidoux/105924088) describes the hill's rock as light-colored quartz monzonite.
